text: Configure an oplog window of at least 24 hours for an ASP change-stream source and longer than the longest expected interruption. The operations guide warns that downtime beyond retention can cause ChangeStreamHistoryLost; 24 hours is not a guarantee for longer outages. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

text: ASP checkpoints initial sync for every supported _id type. Unpredictably ordered identifiers may slow copying without removing checkpoint recovery support. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

text: A checkpoint cannot restore oplog history that has rolled off the source. An outage beyond the retained history can produce ChangeStreamHistoryLost; size the oplog window for acceptable processor downtime. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: Atlas Stream Processing resumable initial sync and source retention

text: If the required resume token has left the oplog by initial-sync completion, ASP fails to avoid data loss. Restarting with resumeFromCheckpoint=false reruns initialSync; checkpoint recovery cannot reconstruct expired oplog history. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: Atlas Stream Processing resumable initial sync and source retention

text: Independent connector evidence supports the retention hazard: Estuary says expired oplog events can require a fresh backfill, while Confluent documents resume failure after the saved token disappears. These describe those connectors, not ASP initial-copy internals. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)
keywords: Atlas Stream Processing resumable initial sync and source retention

text: Confluent's MongoDB Atlas Source Connector guidance also identifies sparse namespace updates as a stale-token risk and recommends connector heartbeat settings. These settings are Confluent connector controls, not documented ASP configuration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-01-13)

text: Checkpoints store source positions rather than copies of source documents. Deleting or expiring source documents after a committed checkpoint does not itself block resumption; retention of the relevant oplog history remains necessary. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: Atlas Stream Processing resumable initial sync and source retention

text: With initialSync enabled, ASP checkpoints both collection copying and subsequent change-event processing. It records an initial oplog position, partitions the copy, and replays changes after copying; interruption can resume from a checkpoint. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: Atlas Stream Processing resumable initial sync and source retention

text: During multi-collection initial sync, a restarted processor skips completed collections and resumes an unfinished collection from its last synchronized document; previously emitted documents can be redelivered. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: Atlas Stream Processing resumable initial sync and source retention

text: Initial-sync recovery is at-least-once: collection-copy or catch-up processing can duplicate documents. Sinks should handle repeated documents idempotently. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
keywords: Atlas Stream Processing resumable initial sync and source retention

text: Default ObjectId or ordered int/long identifiers provide optimal initial-sync performance. Other supported identifiers can extend the copy phase, and a network interruption on a growing partition can prolong it further, increasing exposure to oplog expiry. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
